title: Neural pathology quantification links enlarged brain spaces to vascular amyloid
summary: Convolutional models quantified vascular amyloid and related pathology in donated brain tissue. In 19 cerebral-amyloid-angiopathy cases, enlarged perivascular spaces were associated with amyloid burden in overlying vessels after accounting for other pathology. Paired MRI and histology supported anatomical interpretation. Cross-sectional autopsy findings do not establish impaired clearance as the cause or the sequence of changes.
ai_technology: Aiforia convolutional neural networks; three-dimensional U-Net; SmartInterpol
organization: Massachusetts General Hospital; Harvard Medical School; University College London; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Leiden University Medical Center

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Cross-sectional autopsy tissue quantification, regional MRI/histology comparisons and mixed-effects association analysis in 19 amyloid-angiopathy cases.
evidence.unknown: Causal direction, clearance dynamics and population generalizability remain unestablished; the selected donation cohort was small and automated in-vivo MRI segmentation was not reliable.
evidence.ai_role: Validated CNNs quantify vascular amyloid/fibrin pathology, while learned high-resolution MRI segmentation supports regional anatomical analysis.
